Single Responsibility: each class/module/file has one cohesive responsibility; separate concerns into distinct modules/components. Avoid duplicating logic; refactor repetition into reusable, clearly documented components. Keep design simple, readable, understandable, maintainable, and minimally complex; avoid over-engineering. Implement only currently required functionality. Don't introduce features or code that is not explicitly needed. Focus on delivering working code, not anticipating future requirements.

Apply SOLID: extend without modifying existing code; preserve substitutability; segregate interfaces; depend on abstractions, not low-level modules. Use consistent formatting/style (2-space indentation), meaningful names, descriptive filenames, judicious comments for complex logic, and module organization. Add docstrings to all functions, classes, and modules. Each file is a single unit. Limit files to 180 lines and functions/classes ideally to 60 lines; avoid unnecessary statements/blank lines.

Include a README with a brief overview and clear instructions. Write testable code; achieve minimum 80% coverage; test critical functionality, emphasizing unit tests and using integration tests for component interactions. Refactor regularly, review and improve continuously, and collaborate effectively.

Agent Management: define interfaces for agent creation, deployment, and monitoring. Data Handling: robust validation and error handling. Communication Protocols: mechanisms (e.g., message queues) for agent interaction. Security: consider security implications. Regularly review and update these
